text:
The Canadiens have points in nine straight (7-0-2) and sit at 10-3-3 with 23 points. Our numbers like the team. They aren't sure about the record. Montreal has 49% of the expected goals this season and exactly 50% during the streak, and our model counts six points of luck, a big number this early.

Most of that luck has a name. Jacob Fowler is .938 with 7.7 goals saved above expected over his last five starts, a run that has turned coin-flip nights into wins. Across the season the Habs have allowed five fewer goals than their chances against would predict.

There's real hockey underneath. Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovský make 4.04 expected goals per hour together with 64% of the shot attempts. Phillip Danault's line with Alexandre Texier and Zachary Bolduc has smothered opponents (1.22 expected against per hour, 71% of the chances), even if it's been outscored 3-2. Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson are a 59% pair.

The concerns: the Chris Kreider, Josh Anderson and Alex Newhook line is giving up 4.25 expected goals an hour, and Montreal takes 5.38 penalties a game while the penalty kill leaks 0.89 expected goals a night. The playoff odds (59%) reflect a good team that's been a bit fortunate. Saturday in Toronto, against a Leafs team welcoming back John Tavares, is a fair test.
headline: Montreal's streak rests on Jacob Fowler
